<blog>

# MemoryBlox: Browser-Based Memory Card Game - Comprehensive Project Analysis

## Project Introduction

MemoryBlox is a browser-based memory card matching game inspired by the classic MEMORYBLOX concept. Built with modern web technologies, it provides an engaging puzzle experience with multiple difficulty levels, customizable themes, and rich visual effects. The project demonstrates excellent software engineering practices with its modular architecture, comprehensive testing suite, and extensive configuration management.

### Purpose Statement
MemoryBlox serves as a modern, browser-native implementation of the popular memory card matching game, offering players an immersive experience with smooth animations, responsive design, and competitive scoring system.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- Deliver a polished browser-based memory game with smooth interactions
- Provide multiple difficulty levels and customization options
- Implement a robust scoring system with leaderboards
- Maintain excellent performance across different devices and screen sizes
- Offer extensive configuration capabilities for runtime adjustments

### Target Audience
- Browser-based puzzle game enthusiasts
- Players seeking challenging memory training exercises
- Users interested in customizable gaming experiences

## Technical Architecture

The project follows a clean, layered architecture with clear separation of concerns and well-defined interfaces between components.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Application Entry Point] --> B[Game Engine]
    A --> C[UI Controllers]
    A --> D[Configuration Manager]
    
    B --> E[Game Logic]
    B --> F[Board View]
    B --> G[Gameplay Engine]
    
    C --> H[UI View]
    C --> I[Audio Controller]
    C --> J[Settings Controller]
    
    D --> K[Runtime Config]
    D --> L[Leaderboard Config]
    D --> M[Win Effects Config]
    
    E --> N[Tile Management]
    E --> O[Match Detection]
    E --> P[Game State]
    
    F --> Q[Tile Rendering]
    F --> R[Animation System]
    F --> S[Accessibility Support]
```

### Component Breakdown

The architecture consists of several key layers:

**Core Game Layer**: Manages game state, rules, and logic
**Presentation Layer**: Handles UI rendering and user interactions  
**Configuration Layer**: Manages runtime settings and preferences
**Utility Layer**: Provides shared functionality and helpers

### Design Patterns

The project implements several design patterns:

- **MVC Pattern**: Clear separation between model (game state), view (UI rendering), and controller (event handling)
- **Factory Pattern**: Used for creating game instances and controllers
- **Observer Pattern**: Event-driven communication between components
- **Strategy Pattern**: Pluggable scoring systems and difficulty configurations

### System Relationships

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as UI Controller
    participant Game as Game Engine
    participant Board as Board View
    participant Audio as Audio Manager
    
    User->>UI: Click tile
    UI->>Game: Handle selection
    Game->>Game: Process selection
    Game->>Board: Update state
    Board->>User: Render changes
    Game->>Audio: Play sound effects
```

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
The application bootstraps through `src/index.ts`, which orchestrates the entire game lifecycle and manages component initialization.

### Core Modules

**Game Logic (`src/game.ts`)**: Implements the core game mechanics including tile matching, state management, and win conditions. The module uses immutable state updates and provides comprehensive validation.

**Board Rendering (`src/board.ts`)**: Handles the visual representation of game tiles with 3D effects, animations, and accessibility features. Implements efficient DOM manipulation and lazy rendering for performance.

**Game Engine (`src/gameplay.ts`)**: Provides a facade interface for game operations, enabling easy testing and mocking of game logic.

**Configuration System (`src/runtime-config.ts`)**: Manages runtime configuration loading from `.cfg` files, with comprehensive validation and default fallbacks.

### Configuration Approach
The project uses a sophisticated configuration system with separate files for different aspects:
- `config/ui.cfg`: User interface and visual settings
- `config/leaderboard.cfg`: Scoring and ranking parameters  
- `config/win-fx.cfg`: Visual effect configurations
- `config/shadow.cfg`: Drop shadow effects

### External Dependencies
The project leverages modern web technologies:
- **Vite**: Fast build tool and development server
- **TailwindCSS**: Utility-first CSS framework
- **TypeScript**: Type-safe JavaScript development
- **Playwright**: End-to-end testing framework
- **Vitest**: Unit testing framework

### Integration Points

**Audio System**: Integrated through `src/sound-manager.ts` and `src/audio-ui-controller.ts` for seamless sound effects and music control.

**Leaderboard Integration**: Local storage-based persistence through `src/leaderboard.ts` with configurable scoring algorithms.

**Responsive Design**: Mobile-first approach with adaptive layouts through `src/window-resize.ts` and orientation handling.

### Component Relationships

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AppController {
        +bootstrap()
        +handleTileSelect()
        +render()
    }
    
    class GameplayEngine {
        +selectTile()
        +resolveMismatch()
        +reset()
    }
    
    class BoardView {
        +render()
        +animateMatchedPair()
        +setLayoutConfig()
    }
    
    class SettingsController {
        +initialize()
        +applyChanges()
        +resetPendingToSelected()
    }
    
    AppController --> GameplayEngine
    AppController --> BoardView
    AppController --> SettingsController
    GameplayEngine --> BoardView : updates
```

## Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Multi-Difficulty Gameplay**: Three difficulty levels (Easy, Normal, Hard) with increasing board complexity and scoring multipliers.

**Customizable Themes**: Eight distinct emoji icon packs covering space, nature, food, technology, flags, fantasy, music, and religious symbols.

**Advanced Scoring System**: Dynamic scoring based on time, attempts, difficulty, and special modifiers including portrait mode bonuses and tile multipliers.

**Rich Visual Effects**: Particle systems, confetti animations, and smooth transitions powered by CSS animations and Canvas effects.

### Implementation Highlights

**Performance Optimization**: Lazy loading of tile back-face content, efficient DOM updates, and optimized rendering loops.

**Accessibility Support**: Comprehensive ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and screen reader compatibility.

**Cross-Platform Compatibility**: Responsive design that adapts to desktop, tablet, and mobile devices with orientation awareness.

**Debug Mode**: Special debugging modes for development and testing purposes.

### Feature Architecture

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Menu
    Menu --> DifficultySelect: Start Game
    DifficultySelect --> GameSession: Select Difficulty
    GameSession --> Playing: Begin Match
    Playing --> Matched: Successful Pair
    Playing --> Mismatched: Incorrect Pair
    Matched --> Playing: Continue
    Mismatched --> Playing: Reset Tiles
    Playing --> Win: All Pairs Found
    Win --> Menu: Play Again
    Menu --> Settings: Open Settings
    Settings --> Menu: Apply Changes
```

The project demonstrates exceptional attention to detail in both functionality and architecture, making it an excellent example of modern web application development with strong emphasis on user experience, performance, and maintainability.

**Sources:**
- [index.ts](src/index.ts)
- [game.ts](src/game.ts)
- [board.ts](src/board.ts)
- [difficulty.ts](src/difficulty.ts)
- [icons.ts](src/icons.ts)
- [presentation.ts](src/presentation.ts)
- [gameplay.ts](src/gameplay.ts)
- [runtime-config.ts](src/runtime-config.ts)
- [leaderboard.ts](src/leaderboard.ts)
- [package.json](package.json)
- [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts)

</blog>
